#------------------------------------- code start
# calculate lower and upper band
# for pederobba

data$ped.upper<-data$ped.avg+data$ped.erst

# for treviso

data$tv.upper<-data$tv.avg+data$tv.erst

head(data)

# calculate CD i.e. coefficient of divergence
cd<-round(sqrt(mean(((data$tv.avg-data$ped.avg)/(data$tv.avg+data
$ped.avg))^2)),2)

cd

# set chart

# diagonal line
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+

# points
geom_point(aes(colour=composto), size=2.5)+

# label position
#geom_text(aes(label=composto, x = tv.avg, y = ped.avg),

limits=c(1,10000),breaks=c(1,10,100,1000,10000),formatter="scientific")

breaks=c(1,10,100,1000,10000),formatter="scientific")+

legend.title="composto")+

# background
theme_bw(base_size = 10)+

# scale_colour
scale_colour_hue("composto", h=c(0, 360))+

# facet by the factor
facet_grid(.~subfamily)

> understand the “legend.position” statement under “opts” seems now not
> working at all

This is because you set theme *after* setting opts. So, set theme

Hi,

sorry, actually there is an option named "legend.title", but it does
not one controlling the text of legend title, but controlling the
*style* of legend title.

title label of the legend is determined by
1) name of the scale, by passing e.g., scale_colour_hue("composto",
h=c(0, 360)). so actually you did it.
2) label setting by + labs(x="hoge", colour="composto", etc, etc)
3) specification in aes. so ggplot(aes(colour=hoge)) and (1) and (2)
are undefined, then "hoge" is the legend title of colour.

> how to control the order of facets ? (by default they seem in an
> alfabetical order)

It is same as control the order of legend. Re-level the variable for facet.
